paths.title: 什麼是代理
paths.goal: Distinguish an agent from a plain LLM call, and name the loop that makes it one.
paths.articleHtml:
A language model on its own is a function: text in, text out. An agent wraps that function in a loop that can observe, decide, and act against the world.

The moment a model can call a tool and feed the result back into itself, it stops being a single prediction and becomes a process. This lesson establishes that mental model before we build anything.

  • Model = one prediction.
  • Agent = a controller that repeats predictions with feedback.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
什麼是代理

A language model on its own is a function: text in, text out. An agent wraps that function in a loop that can observe, decide, and act against the world.

The core distinction

The moment a model can call a tool and feed the result back into itself, it stops being a single prediction and becomes a process.

An agent is not a smarter model. It is a dumber model given a loop, tools, and a goal.

Why the loop matters

Each turn, the controller reads the accumulated context, decides on the next action, executes it, and appends the observation. This is the agent loop, and every framework you will meet is a variation on it.

  • Model = one prediction.
  • Agent = a controller that repeats predictions with feedback.

paths.title: 把提示當程式
paths.goal: Treat the system prompt as a contract that shapes behaviour, not as a wish.
paths.articleHtml:
A good system prompt reads like an interface definition: roles, constraints, and the shape of acceptable output. Vague prompts produce vague agents.

We cover role framing, explicit refusal conditions, and how the context window forces you to be economical.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
把提示當程式

A good system prompt reads like an interface definition: roles, constraints, and the shape of acceptable output.

Prompt as contract

State the role, the non-negotiable constraints, and the exact output shape. Then the model has something to conform to.

Budgeting the window

Every token you spend on instructions is a token you cannot spend on the task. The context window is a scarce resource; spend it deliberately.

paths.title: 第一個代理迴圈
paths.goal: Hand-build a minimal think–act–observe loop with no framework.
paths.articleHtml: The boss of the foundations tier: write the loop yourself in ~40 lines, so every abstraction later feels earned rather than magic.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
第一個代理迴圈

The boss of the foundations tier. You will write the loop yourself in about forty lines of code.

The three steps

  1. Think — ask the model for the next action.
  2. Act — execute the chosen tool.
  3. Observe — append the result and repeat.

No framework, no magic. When it works, you own the mental model of the agent loop completely.

paths.title: 工具呼叫
paths.goal: Expose functions to the model with typed schemas and validate what comes back.
paths.articleHtml: Tool calling is how an agent reaches outside its own text. You describe a function with a schema, the model emits a matching call, you run it, and return a structured observation.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
工具呼叫

Tool calling is how an agent reaches outside its own text.

The contract

Describe each function with a JSON schema: name, description, and typed parameters. The description is a prompt — write it for the model, not for humans.

Trust nothing

Validate arguments before executing and never assume the model produced well-formed input. A bad tool call should fail loudly and feed the error back as an observation.

paths.title: 記憶與狀態
paths.goal: Decide what an agent should remember, for how long, and where.
paths.articleHtml: Short-term memory lives in the context window; long-term memory lives in a store you query. Retrieval is just memory you fetch on demand — which leads straight to RAG.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
記憶與狀態

Short-term memory lives in the context window; long-term memory lives in a store you query.

Kinds of memory

  • Working — the current conversation.
  • Episodic — summaries of past sessions.
  • Semantic — facts retrieved by meaning.

Retrieval is just memory you fetch on demand, which leads straight to RAG.

paths.title: 檢索增強生成
paths.goal: Build a retrieval step that grounds the agent in your own documents.
paths.articleHtml: The tier-two boss. Retrieval-augmented generation turns a store of documents into on-demand memory the agent can cite.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
檢索增強生成

The tier-two boss. Retrieval-augmented generation turns a store of documents into on-demand memory.

The pipeline

  1. Chunk and embed your documents.
  2. Embed the query and find nearest chunks.
  3. Inject the chunks into the prompt as grounded context.

Done well, the agent cites sources instead of hallucinating them.

paths.title: 規劃與分解
paths.goal: Let an agent break a goal into ordered sub-tasks before acting.
paths.articleHtml: Planning separates what to do from how. A planner drafts steps; an executor runs them. This split is the seed of multi-agent systems.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
規劃與分解

Planning separates what to do from how.

Plan then execute

A planner drafts an ordered list of steps; an executor runs them one at a time, re-planning when reality disagrees. This split is the seed of multi-agent systems.

paths.title: 多代理協作
paths.goal: Coordinate specialised agents that hand work to one another.
paths.articleHtml: Not yet charted. This lesson will cover supervisor patterns, message passing, and when multiple agents beat one big prompt.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
多代理協作

It will cover supervisor patterns, message passing, and when multiple agents beat one big prompt.

paths.title: 評估與回歸
paths.goal: Measure agent quality with reproducible evals instead of vibes.
paths.articleHtml: You cannot improve what you cannot measure. Evals turn subjective quality into a suite you can run on every change.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
評估與回歸

You cannot improve what you cannot measure.

Building an eval set

Evals turn subjective quality into a reproducible suite: fixed inputs, graded outputs, and a score you can track over time.

paths.title: 護欄與安全
paths.goal: Constrain what the agent can do before it does something you regret.
paths.articleHtml: Draft. Guardrails validate inputs, restrict tools, and add human approval on risky actions.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
護欄與安全

Draft article.

Guardrails validate inputs, restrict which tools are reachable, and insert human approval on risky actions.

paths.title: 自我改進代理
paths.goal: Survey agents that write, test, and refine their own tools.
paths.articleHtml: The frontier tier. Draft survey of self-improving loops and open research questions.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
自我改進代理

The frontier tier — a draft survey.

Agents that author new tools, test them, and fold the successful ones back into their own capability set. Mostly open research for now.

nodes.title: 代理迴圈 · Agent Loop
nodes.bodyHtml:
The agent loop is the observe–decide–act cycle repeated until a goal is met or a budget is spent. It is the single idea that separates an agent from a one-shot model call.

Related: tool calling supplies the act; the context window holds the accumulated observations.

nodes.title: 上下文窗口 · Context Window
nodes.bodyHtml: The context window is the finite span of tokens a model can attend to at once. It is working memory, and it is always scarce.

nodes.title: 工具呼叫 · Tool Calling
nodes.bodyHtml: Tool calling lets a model invoke typed functions. The schema is a contract; the model fills it, you execute it, and the result becomes an observation in the agent loop.

nodes.title: 檢索增強 · RAG
nodes.bodyHtml: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and injects them into the prompt so the model answers from grounded context rather than memory alone.

nodes.title: 多代理 · Multi-Agent
nodes.bodyHtml: Multi-agent systems split a problem across specialised agents that communicate. A supervisor routes; workers execute.

nodes.title: 評估 · Evals
nodes.bodyHtml: Evals are reproducible tests for agent quality: fixed inputs, graded outputs, a tracked score.

nodes.title: 護欄 · Guardrails
nodes.bodyHtml: Guardrails constrain agent behaviour: input validation, tool restriction, and human-in-the-loop approval on risky actions.

paths.title: 二進位與補數
paths.goal: Represent signed integers the way real hardware does.
paths.articleHtml: Everything above is a lie we agree on. At the bottom there are only bits, and two's complement is how we teach them to count with a sign.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
二進位與補數

Everything above is a lie we agree on. At the bottom there are only bits.

Two's complement

Negate by inverting every bit and adding one. Suddenly subtraction is just addition, and the hardware gets simpler.

paths.title: 邏輯閘
paths.goal: Build arithmetic out of NAND gates alone.
paths.articleHtml: Given only NAND, you can build every other gate, then an adder, then a machine.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
邏輯閘

Given only NAND, you can build every other gate.

From NAND to adder

NOT, AND, OR, XOR — all fall out of NAND. Chain the XORs and carries and you have a ripple-carry adder.

paths.title: 簡單的 CPU
paths.goal: Fetch, decode, execute — the whole loop on paper.
paths.articleHtml: A CPU is a fetch–decode–execute loop wired out of gates and registers.
paths.fullArticleHtml:
簡單的 CPU

A CPU is a fetch–decode–execute loop wired out of gates and registers.

nodes.title: 位元 · Bits
nodes.bodyHtml: A bit is one binary digit. Everything else is agreement about how to group and interpret them.

nodes.title: 邏輯閘 · Logic Gates
nodes.bodyHtml: Logic gates compute boolean functions in hardware. NAND alone is functionally complete.
